internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 2851 occurrences is either the common noun ilah / plural aliha ("a deity / deities," 147 = form N) or the proper name Allah / vocative Allahumma ("God," 2704 = form PN). Both surface families denote the same thing at bottom: a being named as a god. Allah is the one true deity (the sole legitimate ilah); the plural aliha are the false gods the idolaters name and worship; the negated singular in "la ilaha illa..." asserts there is no deity but the one; the interrogative "a-ilahun maʕa llah" ("is there a deity alongside Allah?") challenges rival deity-claims. In each, once you subtract case/number, proclitics (wa-, bi-, li-, ta-, fa-), interrogative hamza, and construction, what remains is the same residue: "that which is (taken as) a god."
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM/number: singular ilah vs dual ilahayn vs plural aliha carry only count, not root meaning. CLITICS: wa-/bi-/li-/ta-/fa- prefixes and the interrogative hamza (a-ilahun) are syntactic, stripped off. CONSTRUCTION: the tawhid frame "la ilaha illa X" contributes the exclusive-negation scaffolding; the residue inside it is still bare "deity." CONTEXT/participants: true vs false referent (Allah vs idols) is supplied by the surrounding clause and the speaker's stance, NOT by the root — the root is neutral as to whether the deity is real. LEXICALIZATION LAYER (the one real subtlety): in the proper name Allah the descriptive "deity" content is frozen into a rigid designator whose primary synchronic job is reference. That referential function is a lexicalization layer sitting ON TOP of the deity residue, not a replacement of it — the residue is still recoverable internally because the Quran predicates ilah-hood of Allah ("la ilaha illa llah") and contrasts Allah against the aliha.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The proper name Allah itself (2704 occurrences, ~95% of the data). One can argue a rigid-designator proper name has subtracted its descriptive residue entirely, leaving pure reference — the way "God" as a personal name need not actively predicate "is a deity." If that view is taken, the deity residue is not DEMONSTRABLY present in the bulk of occurrences but only etymologically assumed, and universal presence would rest on an unverifiable claim about a frozen name. This does not surface as an incoherent occurrence (no verse uses Allah to mean anything non-divine), but it is the point where the residue is weakest / least independently observable.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: That the packet conflates two things QAC's shared root-tag masks: (a) a live common noun ilah/aliha carrying the deity residue, and (b) a lexically-independent proper name Allah that is synchronically underived (the classical dispute: Allah from al-ilah by contraction vs. Allah as a primitive name). Under this competitor there is no single root contribution spanning all 2851 — there is a deity noun (147) plus a rigid name (2704) that merely shares consonants. Internal evidence pushes back: "la ilaha illa llah" and "a-ilahun maʕa llah" put the name and the common noun in the same predication/contrast, showing the tradition treats Allah as THE ilah, so the residue does bridge both — but the competitor cannot be refuted from internal evidence alone.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Residue is distinctive against nearest roots: r-b-b (lord/master/nurturer) is relational authority and care; ʕ-b-d (worship/servitude) is the act and the worshipper's stance; ḥ-m-d/s-b-ḥ are praise/glorification. Alh alone names the deity-entity as such — the object-of-worship qua god. Falsifiable: an Alh occurrence meaning something outside the deity field (e.g., the classical etyma waliha "bewilderment/distraction" or aliha "to take refuge/be devoted") would break the unity; none of the 2851 packet occurrences show any such non-deity sense — all are ilah/aliha/Allah.
internal_discovery.rationale: Full coverage assessed by clustering all 2851 occurrences: 147 form-N (ilah singular incl. interrogative a-ilahun, dual ilahayn, plural aliha, ~42 in the "la ilaha illa" negation frame, ~36 in false-gods plural context) and 2704 form-PN (Allah with proclitics wa-/bi-/li-/ta-/fa- and vocative Allahumma). The ~9 apparent stray PN tokens (al-rahim, al-rahman, min, etc.) are pure token-position artifacts from the basmala prefix in verse_text, not real anomalies — each word_ref lands on Allah. After subtracting form, number, clitics, the interrogative hamza, and the negation construction, a single non-empty residue remains in EVERY occurrence: "deity / object taken as a god." True-vs-false referent is context-supplied, not root-supplied, so false-god occurrences are consistent (they ARE named as deities). No occurrence carries a non-deity sense, so nothing is left unreconciled — universal presence holds. I set strength to MODERATE rather than STRONG for one honest reason: ~95% of the data is the proper name Allah, where the deity residue is lexicalized into a rigid designator and is only INTERNALLY retrievable (via "la ilaha illa llah" and Allah-vs-aliha contrasts) rather than independently observable in each token; a rigid-name reading of Allah is a live competing hypothesis that internal evidence cannot fully refute. The residue is distinctive vs r-b-b/ʕ-b-d and falsifiable, but its dependence on the proper-name layer bearing descriptive content caps confidence below STRONG.

adversarial_verification.notes:
COVERAGE: 2851/2851 accounted for. Form inventory: N (ilah/alihah) 147, PN (Allah) 2704.

CLUSTER A — N common noun, 147 occ. Deity-hood is contextually demonstrable in EVERY one; these are literally the word "a god." Sub-constructions all instantiate the deity-slot: (1) tawhid "la ilaha illa X" (2:255; 3:2,6,18; 6:102,106; 20:8,98; 23:116; 27:26; 28:70,88; 37:35; 40:3,62,65; 47:19; 59:22,23; 64:13; 73:9; 9:31; 10:90...) — the deity-category narrowed to one; (2) "ilah wahid" (2:163; 4:171; 14:52; 16:22,51; 18:110; 21:108; 22:34; 37:4; 41:6; 5:73; 6:19; 43:84); (3) false gods "alihah / min duni-llahi ilahan aakhar" (11:53,54,101; 17:42; 18:15; 19:46,81; 21:21-99; 25:3,42; 36:23,74; 37:36,86,91; 38:5,6; 43:45,58; 46:22,28; 71:23; 7:138) — entities SET UP as gods; deity-slot present even though the text DENIES their divinity, exactly as the hypothesis predicts; (4) claimants "inni ilah" (21:29), Pharaoh "ma alimtu lakum min ilahin ghayri / ilahi musa" (28:38; 40:37; 26:29), "ittakhadha ilahahu hawahu" (25:43; 45:23). No N-form failure.

CLUSTER B — PN Allah, 2704 occ. Adversarial crux: a rigid designator, arguably frozen/jamid (nar Allah 104:6; oaths wa-llahi; possessive genitives; "qala llahu"; attribute lists). Refutation attempt: in most PN uses the operative work is bare reference to the specific being, so deity-hood is not a separately-subtractable CONTEXTUAL predication — it rides referentially/etymologically. BUT the hypothesis is explicitly entity-categorial ("names the deity-slot itself... independent of whether affirmed (Allah) or denied") — a property of the referent, not a contextual predicate. That referent's deity-category membership is grounded IN THE PACKET'S OWN VERSES (not external lexicon): 4:171 "innama llahu ilahun wahid," 47:19 & 37:35 "la ilaha illa llah," 3:62/38:65 "wa ma min ilahin illa llah" — the corpus itself predicates ilah of Allah, licensing that the proper name occupies the deity-slot. So no PN occurrence can be shown to LACK deity-hood; reconciliation is direct (the referent IS the god), not forced.

DISTINCTIVENESS (ok): The residue is the deity-slot/object, distinct from r-b-b (lordship: 9:31 contrasts "arbaban" with "ilahan wahidan"; 20:97-98, 6:102 pair rabb and ilah as different) and from ʕ-b-d (worship-act: "uʕbudu llaha ma lakum min ilahin ghayruh" 7:59,65,73,85; 11:50,61,84; 23:23,32 co-occur the act ʕabada with its object ilah as distinct). Alh names the WHAT-is-worshipped, not the relation (rabb) nor the act (ʕabada).

FALSIFIABILITY (true, with caveat): Strongly tested and passing on the 147 common-noun cases (a non-deity sense — e.g. refuge, or a worship-act reading — would refute; none occurs). HONEST RESERVATION: on the 2704 PN occurrences the contribution is near-unfalsifiable because it is true-by-reference (Allah just is the-God); falsifiability is weak there. This weakness does not produce any UNRECONCILED occurrence, so under binary root-unity it does not defeat universal presence — but it should be logged: the claim's real empirical content is carried by Cluster A, and Cluster B is confirmatory-by-reference rather than independently testable.

VERDICT: SUPPORTED. Universal presence of the deity-hood/deity-slot contribution survives the refutation attempt: zero failing occurrences across all 2851; distinctive vs r-b-b and ʕ-b-d; non-empty residue; falsifiable in principle (robustly on the common noun). Nothing canonical.
